source_text.body:
Design an iOS trading app from a prompt in Paper
A designer connected Claude Code to the Paper design tool over MCP and prompted it to create a Robinhood-style iOS stock trading app design on the canvas.
·
Nov 9, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
Felix Lee installed Paper Desktop for Mac, which starts an MCP server whenever a file is open. He linked Claude Code with one terminal command, opened a blank Paper file, and gave a single prompt for a beautiful, simple Robinhood-style iOS stock trading app. The design appeared on the canvas, and he followed up by asking for a stock screen and new colors.
How it went
He says one prompt produced a good-looking app design with no clicking or dragging, and he reports trying the workflow over 100 times. The iteration guidance is behind the paywall, and no metrics are given.
Worth knowing
Paper Desktop must be open with a file loaded. If the connection fails, restart Claude Code and run /mcp to confirm Paper is listed.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Connect to my Paper design file through MCP, then design a [type of app, e.g. iOS stock trading app] on the canvas in the style of [reference app, e.g. Robinhood]. Include [number, e.g. 4] key screens such as [screen list, e.g. home, stock detail, order, portfolio], using consistent colors, type and spacing. Stop when all screens are on the canvas and give me a short list of the design choices you made.
Original source: https://adplist.substack.com/p/a-guide-to-paper-and-claude-code
